newsitem.title: CROATIA: SOCCER-LUCKY LAUDRUP GOAL SNATCHES VICTORY FROM CROATIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LUCKY LAUDRUP GOAL SNATCHES VICTORY FROM CROATIA.

text.p: Croatia had to settle for a 1-1 draw in a crucial World Cup qualifier against Denmark on Saturday after a strong wind diverted a Brian Laudrup cross into the top corner of the net with only eight minutes left.
The home team held the initiative for much of the game but failed to convert any of their chances, especially in the first half, thanks mainly to Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel.
But five minutes into the second half Croatia's top scorer Davor Suker did manage to tip the ball over Schmeichel after a cross by Robert Jarni from the left.
Laudrup's late equaliser got caught up in the strong wind and took Croatian goalkeeper Drazen Ladic by surprise.
Denmark have now drawn level with Greece at the top of group one on seven points but have played one game fewer. Croatia are in third, two points adrift.
"We had more chances and were the better side but we lost two points through an unfortunate goal," Croatian coach Miroslav Blazevic said on TV afterwards.
"But not everything is lost yet -- we have games to play," he added.
Croatia, who beat Denmark 3-0 during the Euro 96 finals in England last summer, were mainly thwarted by Schmeichel in the opening spell.

He first had to stretch to divert a well-taken 25-metre free kick by Aljosa Asanovic in the fourth minute, and then reacted with a reflex save to stop a header by Zvonimir Boban from six metres five minutes later.
The Danes defended with nine players, slowing down the game when they could, but they were powerless to stop Suker scoring five minutes into the second half.
Suker, who scored twice against Schmeichel during Euro 96 scored against him again after a cross by Robert Jarni from the left.
After going behind Denmark began to attack more and created two chances -- the first when Alan Nielsen headed against the post -- and the second being Laudrup's equaliser.
Laudrup sent a high speculative left-foot cross in from the right which was carried by the wind into the top right-hand corner of the net.
"We thought that everything was over after Suker's goal because the defence worked flawlesly," Blazevic said.
Croatia plays neighbouring Slovenia in Split on Wednesday but will be without Suker who misses the match after picking up a second yellow card.
Juventus striker Alen Boksic is also doubtful after going off injured 15 minutes from time.
